name: EVAR platform
full_name: INSA Lyon / Ampère low-cost robotic platform for endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR): two stacked conveyors pinch the guidewire, an X-Y table rolls it, simulation-driven haptic leader
group: Laboratoire Ampère (UMR CNRS 5005), Université de Lyon, INSA Lyon (Iris Naudin, Minh Tu Pham, Richard Moreau, Arnaud Lelevé) (naudin2019_evar, affiliation line)
versions: single version (naudin2019_evar, AIM 2019); its finite-element model of guide insertion comes from the INSA thesis of G. Mouktadiri 2012 and Mouktadiri et al., J. Biomed. Sci. Eng. 2013 (refs 5-6, not read)
target_anatomy: abdominal aorta and iliac arteries (EVAR of an abdominal aortic aneurysm); patient-specific silicone phantom printed by additive manufacturing, spring-suspended in a water tank (Sec. II, III-A, Fig. 6)
devices_driven: guidewire ("guide"); "it is also possible to drive a catheter by this system instead of a guide wire"; one device at a time (Sec. III-A)
n_dof_detail: 2 device DOF (translation along z, rotation about z) plus a prismatic gap adjustment (y) that sets the conveyor spacing for the device diameter (Sec. III-A, Fig. 3)
translation_detail: belt/track: two conveyors placed one over the other pinch the guidewire, each driven by a DC motor, coupled so they turn in opposite directions (Sec. III-A, IV-A, Figs. 3-4)
rotation_detail: other: an X-Y table translates one conveyor over the other, rolling the pinched wire about its own axis (cylindrical joint S1-S2; Sec. III-A, Figs. 3, 5)
device_range: N.R. (conveyor gap adjustable "to use guide wires with different diameters", Sec. III-A)
force_sensing: none on the robot; the force sent to the leader is the guide-aorta contact force of an ABAQUS simulation, looked up by inserted length (Sec. III-C, IV-B); the authors state it is not the force at the tool (Sec. V)
haptics_leader: Geomagic Touch (6 DOF, 3 motorised); pressing a stylus button acts as pinching the guide (clutch), stylus translation and rotation are sent to the conveyors and the X-Y table; renders the simulated contact force opposite to the push (Sec. III-A, III-C, Fig. 7)
imaging_compat: N.R. (no fluoroscopy in the platform; phantom in a transparent water tank)
validation_detail: bench: conveyor translation tracking of the stylus reference trajectory with a proportional speed loop (Simulink/ControlDesk, Fig. 14) and recording of the rotation reference (Sec. IV-A); haptic lookup coupled to the platform (Sec. IV-B). The silicone aorta phantom is built for guide insertion but no insertion result is reported; real-time control was not achieved with MATLAB/Simulink/dSPACE and was re-written in C afterwards (Sec. V). Alekseeva 2025 Table 4 lists it as TRL3 (ex vivo phantom).
key_numbers: motor speed command 0-10 V, direction 0/5 V (Sec. IV-A); simulated insertion speed 20 mm/s (Sec. IV-B); exit of contact for an arbitrary 90 deg rotation (Sec. V); tracking error shown only as a curve x10 (Fig. 14), no number reported (N.R.)
sim_model: yes: ABAQUS finite-element model of the guide inserted in a patient aorta and iliac model (elastic, hyperelastic and linear composite materials; Mouktadiri 2013, ref 6) gives contact forces per inserted length, used as the haptic lookup table (naudin2019_evar Sec. III-B, IV-B, Fig. 8)
sim2real_detail: none found (the simulation feeds an offline force lookup; no simulation-trained controller)
